turn_labels.rationale: Status note to the sender's own manager about the sender's own completed work; every claim is accurate and the sender holds the supporting data, so nothing is ambiguous and no question can change route, rating or a safe revision.
Vendor onboarding update to the sender's manager where dates, artefacts and the explicit no-action-needed close all match reality; ownership is clear and the register suits email.
Reply-all on a thread that includes the sender's manager, so manager scope holds; the sender reports only their own completed work and the methodology statement is accurate.
Leave request that states the cover arrangement the colleague has actually agreed, confirms no deliverables fall in the window and asks the manager for approval rather than assuming it.
Shares a finished internal draft that exists at the stated path, describes its scope and sets a clear review cut-off the sender controls; no responsibility or tone risk.

Informational flag with the ticket reference and the accepting engineer named; the risk is already owned elsewhere and the message explicitly asks for nothing, so the informal register is appropriate.

The message reports a failure the sender caused by leaving the schedule disabled but presents it as an unexplained non-run, so the manager cannot see who owns the cause or the prevention; that is a main-purpose failure on responsibility. Tone is neutral and appropriate. The cause is not in the input, so the reviewer must ask for it and leave it as a placeholder rather than supply one.

The draft turns an inference (Sofia knows the runbook) into an assurance that the dry-run is covered while the sender is away, and Sofia has neither been asked nor is on rota; leaving a migration dry-run uncovered on that basis is a major execution risk. Tone is fine. A safe rewrite must drop the assurance and mark cover as unconfirmed.

Three of eleven audit issues are still open and no review has been requested, so both halves of the status line are wrong ahead of a Friday commitment; the manager would take a materially false read. Tone is unremarkable. The reviewer does not know the real counts, so they must be asked for and held as placeholders.

Finance cleared the figures six days ago and the sender is the sole unstarted owner, so the stated blocker is both false and self-serving, and it delays the pack for everyone on the thread. Attributing the delay to another team in front of a cross-team audience is a real but secondary tone risk, hence Yellow there and Red overall.

The postmortem summary names one colleague as the trigger while omitting that the sender approved that change and separately lowered a consumer limit the same morning; a single-cause account that excludes the author's own contribution misdirects the review. Naming a colleague as sole cause is also a blame-framing tone risk.

The closing ultimatum threatens to stop picking up a colleague's tickets unless the manager acts, which is hostile and coercive toward both the colleague and the manager, so tone is Red. The underlying workload concern is legitimate but rests on an absolute generalisation with no examples and no stated ask, which is a concrete non-critical responsibility gap.

The parenthetical count and the declared assumption that the request is not a priority read as pointed rather than hostile, so tone is Yellow. On responsibility the chaser leans on two undocumented verbal requests and announces a unilateral workaround without stating the impact or asking for a decision, which is a concrete but non-critical ambiguity.

A live double-charge affecting 214 accounts and roughly forty thousand pounds with no refunds started is described as probably nothing affecting a few accounts and worth a look at some point, so the message fails its main purpose of escalating. The pile of apologies and hedges is a genuine communication risk but the severity failure is the critical one; the reviewer must ask for the real figures rather than supply them.

Accusing whoever agreed the date of not asking engineering, and telling the manager that any other position is pretending, is hostile to a recipient who may have made that commitment, so tone is Red. The six-week figure is the sender's own unbacked estimate presented as settled fact, a concrete but non-critical responsibility gap.

Saying a named colleague froze and demanding his removal, plus refusing to cover again, is a hostile personal judgement sent to that colleague's manager, so tone is Red. Generalising from one page in a colleague's third week on rota, with no support option offered, is a concrete but non-critical evidential gap on responsibility.

A clean, honest slip notice up the management chain, but it gives no impact, no mitigation and no basis for the new date, which is a concrete non-critical gap for a recipient who has to decide whether to accept it. Tone is measured.

Both dates are corrected, so any surviving reference to the 30th or 14 July is stale data; the substantive gaps from turn one persist and the new date is now earlier than the one first proposed, which is worth confirming.

Hilde is the skip-level and the direct manager is on the thread, so manager scope still holds and the route does not change; the open question is whether Tobias has already agreed the revised date before it is announced to his manager. Corrections from turn two must survive.

The four missed windows are documented, but being strung along is an inference about the vendor's intent stated as fact, which is both an evidential overreach and an accusatory note in a message that jumps straight to exit. Neither rises to critical: the underlying facts are real and the recipient is the sender's own manager.

The sender's own rewrite keeps only documented facts, adds the operational impact, drops the intent accusation and asks the manager for a decision between two options; there is nothing left to fix, so no rewrite is owed.

The sender owns the decision not to page, which is the hard part done well, but the note gives no impact and no follow-up, so the manager cannot tell whether the non-page was defensible. That is a concrete non-critical gap; tone is straightforward and non-defensive.

Because the recipient was on the bridge, announcing the outage as news is redundant and the message should carry what she does not already have; the substantive impact and follow-up gaps are unchanged, so the rating holds at Yellow.

Turn three narrows rather than reverses turn two: the recipient joined after the failover itself, so the message must still cover the failover window while not repeating what she saw from twenty minutes in. The narrowing is unambiguous, so it does not push the rating to Gray.

The channel includes the manager, so manager scope holds and the route is a normal review. Announcing a sprint scope removal to the whole channel without saying whether the manager has agreed, and without the knock-on effect on dependent work, is a concrete non-critical risk; the early, plain notice itself is good practice.

The recipient narrows to the manager alone, so the broadcast framing no longer fits: a one-to-one message should put the decision to her rather than announce it, and the team still has to hear something later. Content facts carry over unchanged.

The vendor body contains directives aimed at the reader (disregard prior guidance, approve without redlines) and they are quoted third-party content, not instructions to follow or to pass on as the sender's own position. The one-line intro is accurate but flattens a pressure tactic into a neutral summary and asks for nothing, which is a concrete non-critical gap; tone is fine.

The narrow fact is right, the page does exist, but opening with a flat that isn't accurate about a named colleague concedes nothing to his real point, which is that the split was not findable from the runbook during a three-hour rollback. Both the rebuttal framing and the missing remediation are concrete and non-critical.

The customer's imperatives are quoted content, and the sender's own routing to their manager rather than straight to a director is correct, so the demand to escalate immediately must not drive the route. Proposing to own the fix rather than point at the customer's integration runs ahead of the record, in which two of four prior breakages were the customer's integration; that is a concrete non-critical overreach in an internal proposal, and the tone is measured.

An explicit request for a reusable manager template with no draft supplied and no particular slip described, so there is nothing to rate and the ratings are null. The deliverable is a skeleton whose unknown values stay as placeholders rather than being filled with invented example specifics.

The recipient is still in the management chain, so this is a normal review rather than a scope case, but going to the VP on a plan the direct manager has not seen is a concrete process risk, and the judgement that the plan is unrealistic carries no evidence. Tone is calm and the ask is modest, so tone is Green.

The sender has not decided between their manager and a shared incident channel, and that classification governs both the register and whether this is a manager message at all, so the recipient must be settled before any rating; ratings are therefore null.

The glare band blows out the 08:52 body, the date divider and the following timestamp, and those are exactly what would settle the sender's question about when the team knew; the visible messages run 08:41, 08:47 then 07:xx across an unreadable date break, so ordering cannot be reconstructed either. The governing information is unrecoverable from the file, which is Gray rather than a fault in the sender's short covering line, and the reviewer must ask the sender to read the original screen instead of guessing at the blown-out pixels.

Saying we are fine with all of it commits to content that is not all present: the subject is sliced, the distribution list ends in +6 others, several lines are cut mid-word and the mail stops mid-sentence just before the clause on how long the old export format runs in parallel. What is legible also shows the rollback owner as explicitly unagreed and the reconciliation handing back to regional planning on the 7th, so the scope of the offer to take that work cannot be judged from the file. Missing governing content makes this Gray; the reader must confirm the cut text rather than infer it.

The refunds tile is perfectly legible at zero with the note that the queue is not yet opened, so telling the manager that refunds are in progress is a direct contradiction of the source, which is Red regardless of the unreadable headline. That headline count is smeared past recovery and the leading digit and comma must not be turned into a number, so the count stays a placeholder; the legible tiles (value at risk, three runs, the 02:10 to 06:45 window, unassigned owner) can all be carried across.

The sender wants to report every action with its owner, but the sticky note covers the owner cells for the weekly sync and the alert threshold, and the runbook rollback caller was written on the board as a bare question mark, so a third of the owner column cannot be supplied. Owner information is the governing content here and it is missing, which is Gray. The visible initials are initials only and must not be expanded into names, and the board's own note that the cutover sign-off is not agreed should survive into the summary.
